plan.note: Coordinates are pixels on the Museum's own ground-floor plan (1600 x 2209, dated 03/2026). Our drawing follows its layout; it is not to scale.

hours: Galleries 10.00–17.00 daily (Fridays to 20.30). Great Court 10.00–17.30 (Fridays to 20.30). Closed 24–26 December.

spaces.name: Enlightenment
spaces.note: The 18th century: new knowledge, scientific discovery, European colonialism and the transatlantic slave trade.

spaces.name: Collecting the world
spaces.note: The collectors who have shaped the Museum since it opened in 1759.

spaces.name: The Waddesdon Bequest
spaces.note: Nearly 300 medieval and Renaissance pieces left to the Museum in 1898 by Baron Ferdinand Rothschild.

spaces.name: Free displays
spaces.note: Short free displays, just inside the Main entrance.

spaces.name: Egyptian sculpture
spaces.note: Three thousand years of pharaonic sculpture, including the Rosetta Stone and the colossal bust of Ramesses II.

spaces.name: Assyrian sculpture and Balawat Gates
spaces.note: Rooms 6a and 6b: colossal winged lions from Nimrud and the bronze gates of Shalmaneser III from Balawat, 1100–800 BC.

spaces.name: Assyria: Nimrud
spaces.note: Rooms 7–8: carved panels from the Northwest Palace of Ashurnasirpal II (883–859 BC) at Nimrud.

spaces.name: Assyria: Nimrud
spaces.note: Rooms 7–8: carved panels from the Northwest Palace of Ashurnasirpal II (883–859 BC) at Nimrud.

spaces.name: Assyria: Nineveh
spaces.note: Carved panels from Sennacherib's Southwest Palace at Nineveh, 704–692 BC.

spaces.name: Assyria: Lion hunts, Siege of Lachish and Khorsabad
spaces.note: Three rooms, 10a to 10c: Ashurbanipal's lion hunts, the siege of Lachish and Sargon II's palace at Khorsabad, 710–635 BC.

spaces.name: Greece: Minoans and Mycenaeans
spaces.note: Bronze Age Crete, the Cyclades, Greece and the Troad, 3200–1100 BC.

spaces.name: Greece 1050–520 BC
spaces.note: Greece's revival after the collapse of Mycenaean palace society.

spaces.name: Greek vases
spaces.note: Athenian pottery of 530–500 BC, when painters took up the red-figure technique.

spaces.name: Greece: Athens and Lycia
spaces.note: Athens after the Persian wars, 520–430 BC: democracy, the human body and the Athenian empire.

spaces.name: Greece: Bassai sculptures
spaces.stepNote: This gallery has no level or lift access.
spaces.note: The frieze from the Temple of Apollo Epikourios at Bassai, 420–400 BC.

spaces.name: Nereid Monument
spaces.note: A Lycian tomb from Xanthos, in south-west Turkey, built about 390–380 BC.

spaces.name: Greece: Parthenon
spaces.note: Sculptures from the Parthenon in Athens, 447–432 BC.

spaces.name: Greece: Parthenon
spaces.note: Fragments of the Parthenon sculptures and pieces of the building's architecture.

spaces.name: Greece: Parthenon
spaces.note: Fragments of the Parthenon sculptures and pieces of the building's architecture.

spaces.name: Greece: Athens
spaces.note: Sculpture and architecture of Athens, 430–400 BC.

spaces.name: Greeks and Lycians 400–325 BC
spaces.note: Private luxury in an age of political change, with the Tomb of Payava.

spaces.name: Mausoleum of Halikarnassos
spaces.note: Sculpture from the tomb at Halikarnassos, about 350 BC.

spaces.name: The world of Alexander
spaces.note: Alexander the Great and the Hellenistic world, about 323–31 BC.

spaces.name: Greek and Roman sculpture
spaces.note: Roman statues of 100 BC–AD 200, many based on Greek originals.

spaces.name: Living and Dying
spaces.note: How people everywhere deal with life and death. The north end meets the North stairs and lift up from the Montague Place entrance.

spaces.name: North America
spaces.note: Native North American cultures from 11000 BC to the present.

spaces.name: Mexico
spaces.note: Olmec, Maya, Aztec and Mixtec works, from about 2000 BC to the Spanish conquest in 1521.

spaces.name: Special exhibitions
spaces.note: The Sainsbury Exhibitions Gallery.

spaces.name: Great Court
spaces.note: The covered square at the centre of the Museum, under a glass and steel roof of 3,312 panes. Open 10.00–17.30 (Fridays to 20.30).

spaces.name: Reading Room
spaces.note: The former Reading Room of the British Library, opened in 1857; its readers included Bram Stoker, Arthur Conan Doyle and Lenin. The viewing area faces the south side of the Great Court.

spaces.name: Entrance hall
spaces.note: Just inside the Main entrance: the cloakroom, the South stairs, the Grenville Room shop and Room 3.

spaces.name: West stairs hall
spaces.note: Behind the Great Court on the left, through Rooms 29a and 29b. The West stairs and West lift go up to the Members' Room and the upper floors.

spaces.name: East stairs landing
spaces.note: Behind the Great Court on the right, between Rooms 27 and 1. The stairs display 19th-century plaster casts of ancient sculpture.

spaces.name: Pizzeria
spaces.note: In the south-west corner, past Room 12.

doors.note: Stairs or the level access lift

points.name: Main entrance, Great Russell Street
points.note: Across the forecourt and up 12 steps with a handrail. For step-free entry, use the lifts on either side of the steps.

points.name: Montague Place entrance
points.note: The north entrance, one level down (Level -1). It is step-free: the North lift is on the left past the bust of King Edward VII, with 12 steps to its right, up to Room 24 and the Great Court.

points.name: Rosetta Stone
points.note: The key to deciphering the ancient Egyptian language and hieroglyphic script.

points.name: Parthenon sculptures
points.note: On permanent display since 1817. The frieze shows the procession of the Panathenaic festival, Athena's birthday.

points.name: Assyrian Lion Hunt reliefs
points.note: Carved for King Ashurbanipal's palace at Nineveh, 645–635 BC. Hunting lions was the sport of Assyrian kings.

points.name: Hoa Hakananai'a
points.note: A colossal ancestor figure (moai) from Rapa Nui/Easter Island. The Museum gives its name as 'lost or stolen friend'.

points.name: Holy Thorn Reliquary
points.note: Gold, enamel, rubies, pearls and sapphires around a single thorn, made in Paris about 1400 for Jean, duc de Berry.

points.name: Winged bulls from Khorsabad
points.note: A pair of colossal human-headed winged bulls that guarded the palace of King Sargon II at Khorsabad. They greet visitors to Room 10a.

points.name: Winged lions from Nimrud
points.note: Two colossal winged human-headed lions that flanked an entrance to the palace of Ashurnasirpal II (883–859 BC) at Nimrud.

points.name: Nereid Monument
points.note: The largest and finest of the Lycian tombs from Xanthos, rebuilt in Room 17.

points.name: Mausoleum of Halikarnassos
points.note: Regarded as one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World; the word 'mausoleum' comes from it.

points.name: Information Desk
points.note: 10.00–17.00. Free paper maps.

points.name: Guide Desk
points.note: 10.00–16.30. Sells earbuds for the Audio app.

points.name: Families Desk
points.note: 10.00–12.30 and 13.15–16.30, weekends and Camden school holidays only.

points.name: Visitor and Member cloakroom
points.note: 10.00–17.00 (Fridays to 20.30). Last deposit one hour before closing.

points.name: Toilets (Great Court, west)
points.note: With an accessible toilet beside them.

points.name: Toilets (Great Court, east)
points.note: With an accessible toilet and baby changing.

points.name: Toilets (East stairs)
points.note: With an accessible toilet and baby changing.

points.name: Court Café (west)
points.note: Sandwiches, salads, cakes and hot drinks at long sharing tables. 10.00–17.00.

points.name: Court Café (north-east)
points.note: Sandwiches, salads, cakes and hot drinks at long sharing tables. 10.00–17.00.

points.name: Pizzeria
points.note: Hand-tossed pizzas, salads and gelato; gluten-free bases. 11.00–16.00. For assisted disabled access, ask a member of staff.

points.name: Forecourt Café
points.note: Food trucks with outdoor seating, 10.00–17.00; hours may change in poor weather.

points.name: Main entrance lifts
points.note: Level access lifts on both sides of the entrance steps.

points.name: Great Court lifts
points.note: Near the Great Court Shop, on both sides of the Reading Room.

points.name: South lifts
points.note: By the front entrance to the Great Court.

points.name: West lift
points.note: Up to the Members' Room on Level 1 and the upper floors.

points.name: North lift
points.note: Down to the Montague Place entrance; up to the upper floors.

points.name: North stairs
points.note: Down to the Montague Place entrance; up to the upper floors.

points.name: Great Court central staircase
points.note: Curves up round the Reading Room to the Great Court Restaurant on Level 3.

points.name: Stairs down to the Clore Centre
points.note: The Clore Centre for Education is open to the public only for events; the Ford Centre for Young Visitors is down here too, at weekends and in school holidays.
